```{r knitr-options, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE,
                      fig.align = "center")
```

**Exploratory analysis. None of the five registrations contains a pooled
model across studies. This analysis was specified on 9 October 2026, after the
registered results of all five studies were known (Study 1 on 7 October 2026;
Studies 2 to 5 on 8 October 2026), and nothing in it changes a registered
verdict.**

# 0. What this file does

In Study 1, telling participants that the artist Alex made an artwork by
prompting an AI system lowered its rated creativity by 0.448 points on a
five-point scale. Studies 2, 4 and 5 then showed participants second works
that Alex made by hand from such a first artwork, at three levels of
modification: None (the first work shown again unchanged), Slight (colour and
contrast adjustments) and Dramatic (substantial changes by hand). Each study
estimated the source penalty, the Human minus AI difference in the ratings of
the second work, at each level. Each did so on its own sample, so none could
say with much precision what shape the penalty takes as modification grows.
This file pools the three studies to ask that question.

Three accounts predict different shapes. If an AI origin taints whatever is
built on it, the penalty is the same at every level (taint). If raters judge
only what Alex added, there is no penalty at any level (severance). If raters
credit Alex less when more of the second work still comes from the first, the
penalty is largest at None and shrinks as modification grows (discounting).
The program memorandum of 4 September 2026 proposed this comparison as an
exploratory "propagation curve" (`Docs/Study 2/AI_Art_Copyright_Program_Memorandum.md`,
Part IV.D), and said that the None level discriminates among the accounts.

**Status.** The analysis is exploratory. None of the five registrations in
`Docs/Preregistration/AsPredicted/` contains a pooled model across studies. It
was specified on 9 October 2026, after the registered results of Study 1 (7
October 2026) and of Studies 2 to 5 (8 October 2026) were known, and nothing in
it changes a registered verdict. Every p-value below is uncorrected, that is,
not adjusted for the number of tests run, and carries no verdict. The
memorandum proposed comparing the accounts as nested models, each adding terms
to the one before, scored by leave-one-out cross-validation, which asks how
well a model predicts each observation from a fit that leaves that observation
out. Section 7 compares the same nested models by likelihood-ratio tests and
by two information criteria, scores of fit with a charge for each parameter;
one of them, AIC, approximates the leave-one-out score in large samples.

This file:

1. reads each study's deposited long data file and checks that it carries the
   real labels and reproduces the study's registered analysed sample
   (section 2);
2. stacks the three derivative studies, keeping each study's own exclusions
   and scoring and dropping the six-point transformativeness items as each
   study's primary analysis does (section 3);
3. fits one pooled model per measure and estimates the penalty at each level,
   pooled over studies and within each study (section 4), its trend across
   the levels (section 5) and whether it lies inside the registered
   equivalence bound of plus or minus 0.224 rating points (section 6);
4. compares the three accounts as nested models (section 7);
5. sets the creativity penalty on original artworks, from Studies 1 and 3,
   beside the penalty on second works (section 8), and draws the figures
   (section 9);
6. checks the pooled penalties with an ordinal model, one that treats the five
   answers as ordered categories, with each study left out in turn, against
   each study's own registered estimates, and within each time level of
   Studies 4 and 5 (section 10);
7. records the status of every fit, says what the numbers show, and records
   the run (sections 11 to 13).

Creativity comes first and is the primary measure, because it is the one
measure rated for original artworks and second works alike. Transformativeness
and essence change follow.

Four limits apply throughout.

- Study 2's creativity item carried no definition, while Studies 4 and 5 used
  Study 1's definition. Study 2's registration says that creativity
  comparisons across studies are exploratory for that reason.
- At None the second work is the first unchanged, and the creativity question
  asks how much creativity went into producing it. Ratings there sit near the
  bottom of the scale (section 4 gives the means), which leaves little room
  for a penalty to show. The None level therefore discriminates less sharply
  than the memorandum assumed.
- Study 4 also varied source time (the hours Alex is said to have spent on the
  first artwork) and Study 5 editing time (the hours he is said to have spent
  on the second). The pooled model leaves both out and so averages over them.
  Section 10.4 reads each study's registered tests of these factors and shows
  the penalty at each time.
- Each study counts once in a pooled estimate, whatever its size.

# 1. Setup

## 1.1 Packages

```{r packages}
# dplyr, tidyr, tibble and readr build and write the tables. jsonlite reads
# the three survey files. lme4 fits the linear mixed models and lmerTest
# supplies Satterthwaite degrees of freedom. emmeans gives estimated marginal
# means and the contrasts between them. ordinal fits the cumulative-link mixed
# model of section 10. ggplot2 draws the figures and knitr prints the tables.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(readr)
  library(lme4)
  library(lmerTest)
  library(emmeans)
  library(ordinal)
  library(ggplot2)
})
```

## 1.3 Run record and table helpers

```{r run-record}
# The run record ties every output to this run. It stores the SHA-256
# checksum of each input (a 64-character fingerprint of the file's exact
# bytes), deletes the previous run's manifest now, deletes each output's
# previous copy before the chunk that writes it, and writes the manifest last.
# A manifest on disk therefore means the run reached its end. The figure
# copies in the manuscript folder are listed under their own label.
run <- start_run_record(
  IN, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "crossstudy_run_manifest.csv"), CROSS_DIR,
  other_dirs = c("Docs/Writing/Final Paper/figures" = PAPER_FIG_DIR))
cat("Run identifier:", run$run_id, "\n")

# Every table, the run record's included, carries the analysis status in its
# last column, so a table read on its own still says what it is.
table_path <- function(name) file.path(OUT_TABLES, name)
write_table <- function(df, name) {
  readr::write_csv(mutate(df, analysis_status = ANALYSIS_STATUS),
                   table_path(name), na = "NA")
}
# The input record: one row per input file, with its size and checksum.
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("crossstudy_run_inputs.csv"))
write_table(run$inputs, "crossstudy_run_inputs.csv")
# Every table printed in this report opens its caption with the same status.
show_table <- function(df, caption, digits = 3) {
  knitr::kable(df, digits = digits, caption = paste(CAPTION_LEAD, caption))
}

# The fit log collects one row per model fitted in this file. Section 11
# writes it.
fit_log <- list()
log_fit <- function(status, role, measure, model, d, max_abs_gradient = NA_real_) {
  fit_log[[length(fit_log) + 1]] <<- tibble(
    role = role, measure = measure, model = model, n_obs = nrow(d),
    fit_error = status$fit_error, converged = status$converged,
    singular = status$singular, usable = fit_usable(status),
    max_abs_gradient = max_abs_gradient,
    messages = if ("lme4_messages" %in% names(status)) status$lme4_messages
               else status$messages)
}
```

```{r read-inputs}
read_long <- function(path) {
  readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE, guess_max = 1e6)
}
long <- list(
  "Study 1" = read_long(IN[["study1_long"]]),
  "Study 2" = read_long(IN[["study2_long"]]),
  "Study 3" = read_long(IN[["study3_long"]]),
  "Study 4" = read_long(IN[["study4_long"]]),
  "Study 5" = read_long(IN[["study5_long"]]))

# A file is the one a study's real run wrote when its checksum equals the one
# listed in the run manifest in that study's tables/ folder. A blind run
# writes its manifest to tables/blind_run/ instead, so a match here can only
# come from a real run. Study 1 had no blind mode.
manifest_row <- function(manifest_path, label, path) {
  m <- readr::read_csv(manifest_path, show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
  row <- m[m$file == label, ]
  sha <- unname(tools::sha256sum(path))
  nrow(row) == 1 && isTRUE(as.logical(row$written_this_run)) &&
    identical(row$sha256, sha)
}
check <- function(study, quantity, expected, observed) {
  tibble(study = study, quantity = quantity,
         expected = as.character(expected), observed = as.character(observed),
         pass = identical(as.character(expected), as.character(observed)))
}
n_people <- function(d) n_distinct(d$id)
n_five   <- function(d) sum(d$k_points == 5 & !is.na(d$rating))
n_six    <- function(d) sum(d$k_points == 6 & !is.na(d$rating))
all_real <- function(d) "label_mode" %in% names(d) && all(d$label_mode == "real")

input_checks <- bind_rows(

## 2.2 The three derivative studies showed the same images

```{r image-check}
# The pooled model gives each source image and each second work one
# intercept shared by all three studies, which is right only if the studies
# showed the same images. Each survey file names the image graphic that each
# question displays. The check reads every question that displays a graphic
# and requires the same questions to display the same graphics in all three
# surveys.
survey_images <- function(qsf) {
  q <- jsonlite::fromJSON(qsf, simplifyVector = FALSE)
  rows <- lapply(q$SurveyElements, function(el) {
    if (!identical(el$Element, "SQ")) return(NULL)
    text <- el$Payload$QuestionText
    tag  <- el$Payload$DataExportTag
    if (is.null(text) || is.null(tag)) return(NULL)
    ims <- regmatches(text, gregexpr("IM_[A-Za-z0-9]+", text))[[1]]
    if (length(ims) == 0) return(NULL)
    tibble(tag = tag, graphics = paste(ims, collapse = " "))
  })
  bind_rows(rows) %>% distinct() %>% arrange(tag, graphics)
}
images <- lapply(c("Study 2" = "study2_survey", "Study 4" = "study4_survey",
                   "Study 5" = "study5_survey"),
                 function(k) survey_images(IN[[k]]))
same_images <- identical(images[["Study 2"]], images[["Study 4"]]) &&
  identical(images[["Study 2"]], images[["Study 5"]])
cat("Questions that display a graphic, per survey:",
    paste(vapply(images, nrow, integer(1)), collapse = ", "),
    "| distinct graphics:", n_distinct(images[["Study 2"]]$graphics), "\n")

# The ten source images also carry the same names in the three long files.
image_names <- list(sort(unique(long[["Study 2"]]$image)),
                    sort(unique(long[["Study 4"]]$source)),
                    sort(unique(long[["Study 5"]]$image)))
same_names <- length(image_names[[1]]) == 10 &&
  identical(image_names[[1]], image_names[[2]]) &&
  identical(image_names[[1]], image_names[[3]])

input_checks <- bind_rows(
  input_checks,
  check("Studies 2, 4 and 5", "the same questions display the same graphics in the three surveys",
        TRUE, same_images),
  check("Studies 2, 4 and 5", "the ten source images carry the same names in the three long files",
        TRUE, same_names))
```

```{r write-input-checks}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("crossstudy_input_checks.csv"))
write_table(input_checks, "crossstudy_input_checks.csv")
show_table(input_checks, "Table 2.1. Every input check. The run stops if any fails.")
if (!all(input_checks$pass)) stop("Some input disagrees with its study's registered sample.")
```

# 3. The pooled data

```{r pooled-data}
# One row per participant, second work and measure from the three derivative
# studies. The columns are named differently across studies: in Study 4 the
# column source names the source image and label names Human or AI, while
# Studies 2 and 5 call these image and source. Each column is picked by name.
pool_study <- function(d, study, source_col, image_col) {
  tibble(study = study, id = d$id, source = d[[source_col]], image = d[[image_col]],
         modification = d$modification, measure = d$dimension,
         k_points = d$k_points, rating = d$rating)
}
pooled <- bind_rows(
  pool_study(long[["Study 2"]], "Study 2", "source", "image"),
  pool_study(long[["Study 4"]], "Study 4", "label",  "source"),
  pool_study(long[["Study 5"]], "Study 5", "source", "image")) %>%
  # Each study's primary analysis keeps the five-point items only, so the two
  # six-point transformativeness items are dropped here as there.
  filter(k_points == 5, !is.na(rating)) %>%
  mutate(study        = factor(study, levels = DERIV_STUDIES),
         source       = factor(source, levels = SOURCE_LEVELS),
         modification = factor(modification, levels = MOD_LEVELS),
         measure      = factor(measure, levels = MEASURES),
         id           = factor(id),
         image        = factor(image))
stopifnot(!anyNA(pooled$study), !anyNA(pooled$source),
          !anyNA(pooled$modification), !anyNA(pooled$measure))

# The rows analysed in each study equal its registered analysed ratings.
rows_by_study <- count(pooled, study)
stopifnot(identical(rows_by_study$n, c(20659L, 6178L, 11768L)))

# Numeric codes for the model comparison of section 7. src is +1 for Human
# and -1 for AI, as sum-to-zero contrasts code the source. st1 and st2 are the
# sum-to-zero codes of the three studies. modlin codes None, Slight and
# Dramatic as -1, 0 and 1 (a straight line), and modquad as 1, -2 and 1 (a
# bend at Slight), so the two together allow any shape across the levels.
pooled <- pooled %>%
  mutate(src     = ifelse(source == "Human", 1, -1),
         st1     = unname(c("Study 2" = 1, "Study 4" = 0, "Study 5" = -1)[as.character(study)]),
         st2     = unname(c("Study 2" = 0, "Study 4" = 1, "Study 5" = -1)[as.character(study)]),
         modlin  = unname(c(None = -1, Slight = 0, Dramatic = 1)[as.character(modification)]),
         modquad = unname(c(None = 1, Slight = -2, Dramatic = 1)[as.character(modification)]))
stopifnot(identical(unname(as.matrix(distinct(pooled, study, st1, st2) %>%
                                       arrange(study) %>% select(st1, st2))),
                    unname(contr.sum(3)) * 1))

pooled_counts <- pooled %>%
  group_by(measure, study) %>%
  summarise(participants = n_distinct(id),
            human_participants = n_distinct(id[source == "Human"]),
            ai_participants = n_distinct(id[source == "AI"]),
            ratings = n(), .groups = "drop")
show_table(pooled_counts, "Table 3.1. Participants and analysed ratings in the pooled data.")
```

# 4. The pooled model and the penalty at each level

A linear mixed model is a regression that gives each participant and each
image its own baseline, so that ratings from the same person or of the same
image are not treated as independent. Each measure gets one pooled model:

`rating ~ source * modification * study + (1 | study:id) + (1 | image) + (1 | image:modification)`

The fixed part lets the penalty differ by level and by study. The three
random intercepts give a baseline to each participant within each study, to
each of the ten source images, and to each of the thirty second works (one
image at one level). Every factor uses sum-to-zero contrasts, a coding in
which a factor's effects add to zero across its levels, so each effect is read
against the average of the others. The fit is by restricted maximum likelihood
(REML, the usual estimator of the variances in a mixed model) with the bobyqa
optimizer, the numerical routine that searches for the estimates, as in each
study. Studies 4 and 5 are averaged over their time
factors, which the model leaves out.

An estimated marginal mean is the model's predicted mean for a cell, averaged
equally over the factors not named. The penalty at a level is the Human mean
minus the AI mean at that level. The pooled penalty averages the three
studies' penalties with equal weight. Satterthwaite degrees of freedom are an
approximation to the degrees of freedom a test in a mixed model has. Each
interval is a 95 percent confidence interval, the range of values compatible
with the data at that level.

```{r pooled-fits}
SUM_CONTRASTS  <- list(source = "contr.sum", modification = "contr.sum",
                       study = "contr.sum")
POOLED_RE      <- "(1 | study:id) + (1 | image) + (1 | image:modification)"
POOLED_TEXT    <- paste("rating ~ source * modification * study +", POOLED_RE)
POOLED_FORMULA <- as.formula(POOLED_TEXT)

# fit_with_status() keeps every warning and records whether the fit stopped
# with an error, whether it converged and whether it is singular (a variance
# estimated at zero). Only the contrasts of factors in the formula are passed,
# because lme4 warns about any other and the warning would count as a failure
# to converge.
fit_lmm <- function(formula, d, reml, contrasts) {
  res <- fit_with_status(lmerTest::lmer(
    formula, data = d, REML = reml, contrasts = contrasts,
    control = lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))
  res$data <- d
  res
}
data_by_measure <- setNames(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  pooled %>% filter(measure == m) %>% droplevels()
}), MEASURES)
pooled_fits <- lapply(data_by_measure, function(d) {
  fit_lmm(POOLED_FORMULA, d, reml = TRUE, contrasts = SUM_CONTRASTS)
})
for (m in MEASURES) {
  st <- pooled_fits[[m]]$status
  log_fit(st, "pooled model, REML", m, POOLED_TEXT, data_by_measure[[m]])
  cat(sprintf("%-18s rows %5d | fit error %s | converged %s | singular %s\n",
              m, nrow(data_by_measure[[m]]), st$fit_error, st$converged, st$singular))
  print(lme4::VarCorr(pooled_fits[[m]]$fit))
}
```

A singular fit here is one in which the source-image variance is estimated at
zero: once each second work has its own baseline, the ten source images add no
further spread. A singular fit that converged keeps its numbers.

```{r penalties}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("crossstudy_penalty_by_level.csv"))

# The estimated marginal means of all eighteen cells of source, modification
# and study.
emm_cells <- function(res) {
  do.call(emmeans::emmeans,
          c(list(object = res$fit, specs = ~ source * modification * study,
                 data = res$data), LMER_DF))
}

# Contrast weights are matched to the cells by their labels, so no weight
# depends on the order emmeans lists the cells in. A penalty weight is +1 on
# the Human cell and -1 on the AI cell at the level, in each named study,
# divided by the number of studies named, which gives each study equal weight.
cell_weights <- function(g, level, studies, sign_human = 1, sign_ai = -1) {
  s <- ifelse(g$source == "Human", sign_human, sign_ai)
  as.numeric(g$modification == level) * s *
    as.numeric(g$study %in% studies) / length(studies)
}
penalty_w <- function(g, level, studies) cell_weights(g, level, studies)
mean_w    <- function(g, level, studies, which) {
  cell_weights(g, level, studies, sign_human = as.numeric(which == "Human"),
               sign_ai = as.numeric(which == "AI"))
}

# One row per contrast, with its 95 percent and 90 percent intervals. A fit
# that stopped with an error or did not converge keeps its estimate but loses
# its p-value and intervals.
contrast_rows <- function(emm, weights, status) {
  ct  <- emmeans::contrast(emm, method = weights, adjust = "none")
  s95 <- as_tibble(summary(ct, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), level = 0.95))
  s90 <- as_tibble(summary(ct, infer = c(TRUE, FALSE), level = 0.90))
  lo95 <- intersect(c("lower.CL", "asymp.LCL"), names(s95))
  hi95 <- intersect(c("upper.CL", "asymp.UCL"), names(s95))
  stat <- intersect(c("t.ratio", "z.ratio"), names(s95))
  tibble(contrast    = as.character(s95$contrast),
         estimate    = s95$estimate, se = s95$SE, df = s95$df,
         statistic   = s95[[stat]],
         p_two_sided = na_unless_usable(s95$p.value, status),
         ci95_lo     = na_unless_usable(s95[[lo95]], status),
         ci95_hi     = na_unless_usable(s95[[hi95]], status),
         ci90_lo     = na_unless_usable(s90[[lo95]], status),
         ci90_hi     = na_unless_usable(s90[[hi95]], status))
}

# The scopes of every penalty: the pooled estimate over the studies in the
# fit, then each study on its own.
scopes_of <- function(studies) {
  c(setNames(list(studies), "pooled"), setNames(as.list(studies), studies))
}
penalty_table <- function(res, m, studies) {
  emm <- emm_cells(res)
  g <- as.data.frame(emm@grid)
  scopes <- scopes_of(studies)
  keys <- expand.grid(level = MOD_LEVELS, scope = names(scopes),
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  w_pen <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(keys)), function(i) {
    penalty_w(g, keys$level[i], scopes[[keys$scope[i]]])
  })
  names(w_pen) <- paste(keys$scope, keys$level, sep = " | ")
  w_hum <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(keys)), function(i) {
    mean_w(g, keys$level[i], scopes[[keys$scope[i]]], "Human")
  })
  w_ai <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(keys)), function(i) {
    mean_w(g, keys$level[i], scopes[[keys$scope[i]]], "AI")
  })
  names(w_hum) <- names(w_ai) <- names(w_pen)
  pen <- contrast_rows(emm, w_pen, res$status)
  hum <- contrast_rows(emm, w_hum, res$status)
  ai  <- contrast_rows(emm, w_ai, res$status)
  tibble(measure = m, scope = ifelse(keys$scope == "pooled", "pooled", "within study"),
         study = ifelse(keys$scope == "pooled",
                        paste(studies, collapse = ", "), keys$scope),
         modification = keys$level,
         human_mean = hum$estimate, ai_mean = ai$estimate) %>%
    bind_cols(select(pen, -contrast)) %>%
    mutate(contrast = "Human minus AI", weighting = "each study weighted equally",
           converged = res$status$converged, singular = res$status$singular,
           note = fit_note(res$status), .after = modification)
}

penalties <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  penalty_table(pooled_fits[[m]], m, DERIV_STUDIES)
}))
stopifnot(nrow(penalties) == 3 * 4 * 3)
write_table(penalties, "crossstudy_penalty_by_level.csv")
show_table(penalties %>%
             select(measure, study, modification, human_mean, ai_mean, estimate,
                    se, df, ci95_lo, ci95_hi, p_two_sided),
           paste("Table 4.1. The Human minus AI penalty on each second work, in",
                 "rating points, at each modification level: pooled over Studies 2,",
                 "4 and 5 with equal weight, and within each study, from the pooled",
                 "model. Human and AI means are the model's cell means. Intervals",
                 "are 95 percent; p-values are two-sided and uncorrected."))
```

# 5. The trend of the penalty across the levels

The trend is the slope of the straight line fitted through the three
penalties placed at -1, 0 and 1 for None, Slight and Dramatic: the change in
the penalty for each step up in modification, which equals half of the
Dramatic penalty minus the None penalty. Discounting predicts a negative slope, taint and severance a slope of
zero. The curvature is the Slight penalty minus the mean of the None and
Dramatic penalties: how far the middle level sits off the straight line.

```{r trend}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("crossstudy_penalty_trend.csv"))
trend_table <- function(res, m, studies) {
  emm <- emm_cells(res)
  g <- as.data.frame(emm@grid)
  scopes <- scopes_of(studies)
  w <- list()
  for (sc in names(scopes)) {
    pn <- penalty_w(g, "None", scopes[[sc]])
    ps <- penalty_w(g, "Slight", scopes[[sc]])
    pd <- penalty_w(g, "Dramatic", scopes[[sc]])
    w[[paste(sc, "slope", sep = " | ")]]     <- (pd - pn) / 2
    w[[paste(sc, "curvature", sep = " | ")]] <- ps - (pn + pd) / 2
  }
  rows <- contrast_rows(emm, w, res$status)
  parts <- strsplit(rows$contrast, " | ", fixed = TRUE)
  sc <- vapply(parts, `[`, "", 1)
  tibble(measure = m,
         scope = ifelse(sc == "pooled", "pooled", "within study"),
         study = ifelse(sc == "pooled", paste(studies, collapse = ", "), sc),
         quantity = vapply(parts, `[`, "", 2)) %>%
    mutate(definition = ifelse(quantity == "slope",
                               "change in the penalty per step, (Dramatic minus None) / 2, codes -1, 0, 1",
                               "Slight penalty minus the mean of the None and Dramatic penalties")) %>%
    bind_cols(select(rows, -contrast, -ci90_lo, -ci90_hi)) %>%
    mutate(dramatic_minus_none = ifelse(quantity == "slope", 2 * estimate, NA_real_),
           converged = res$status$converged, singular = res$status$singular,
           note = fit_note(res$status))
}
trends <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  trend_table(pooled_fits[[m]], m, DERIV_STUDIES)
}))
stopifnot(nrow(trends) == 3 * 4 * 2)
write_table(trends, "crossstudy_penalty_trend.csv")
show_table(trends %>% select(measure, study, quantity, estimate, se, df, ci95_lo,
                             ci95_hi, p_two_sided),
           paste("Table 5.1. The slope of the penalty across None, Slight and",
                 "Dramatic (change per step, codes -1, 0, 1) and its curvature at",
                 "Slight, pooled and within each study, in rating points, with 95",
                 "percent intervals and uncorrected two-sided p-values."))
```

# 6. The equivalence reading of the pooled penalty

An equivalence test asks whether a difference lies inside a stated bound. It
runs two one-sided tests: one asks whether the penalty lies above -0.224, the
other whether it lies below +0.224. Both pass at .05 exactly when the 90
percent interval lies inside the bound, and the larger of the two one-sided
p-values is the test's p-value. The bound, plus or minus 0.224 rating points,
is the one Studies 2, 4 and 5 registered: half of Study 1's creativity penalty
of 0.448. A pass means that less than half of that penalty reaches the second
work at that level; it does not mean the penalty is zero. The reading follows
Study 5's registered wording: a penalty is called absent or small only when
the equivalence test passes, and a penalty neither significant nor equivalent
is inconclusive. Here the reading is a description and carries no registered
weight.

```{r equivalence}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("crossstudy_penalty_equivalence.csv"))
tost <- function(est, se, df, bound) {
  p_lower <- pt((est + bound) / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE)
  p_upper <- pt((est - bound) / se, df, lower.tail = TRUE)
  tibble(p_lower = p_lower, p_upper = p_upper, p_tost = pmax(p_lower, p_upper))
}
reading_of <- function(significant, equivalent) {
  case_when(
    is.na(significant) | is.na(equivalent) ~ NA_character_,
    significant & !equivalent  ~ "significant, not inside the bound",
    significant & equivalent   ~ "significant and inside the bound",
    !significant & equivalent  ~ "absent or small: inside the bound",
    TRUE                       ~ "inconclusive: neither significant nor equivalent")
}
equivalence <- penalties %>%
  filter(scope == "pooled") %>%
  select(measure, study, modification, estimate, se, df, ci90_lo, ci90_hi,
         p_two_sided, converged, singular, note) %>%
  bind_cols(tost(.$estimate, .$se, .$df, EQ_BOUND)) %>%
  mutate(bound = EQ_BOUND,
         p_tost = ifelse(is.na(ci90_lo), NA_real_, p_tost),
         equivalent = p_tost < ALPHA,
         interval_inside_bound = ci90_lo > -EQ_BOUND & ci90_hi < EQ_BOUND,
         significant = p_two_sided < ALPHA,
         reading = reading_of(significant, equivalent),
         pass_means = "less than half of Study 1's creativity penalty reaches the second work at this level") %>%
  relocate(bound, .after = ci90_hi)
stopifnot(nrow(equivalence) == 9,
          all(equivalence$equivalent == equivalence$interval_inside_bound, na.rm = TRUE))
write_table(equivalence, "crossstudy_penalty_equivalence.csv")
show_table(equivalence %>% select(measure, modification, estimate, ci90_lo, ci90_hi,
                                  p_tost, p_two_sided, reading),
           paste("Table 6.1. Equivalence of the pooled penalty at each level against",
                 "plus or minus 0.224 rating points, by two one-sided tests on the",
                 "90 percent interval, beside the uncorrected two-sided test."))
```

# 7. The three accounts as nested models

Maximum likelihood (ML) chooses the parameter values under which the observed
ratings are most probable; unlike REML, it lets models with different fixed
effects be compared on the same rows. Four models share the random intercepts
of section 4 and the modification by study part, which lets the average rating
at each level differ by study. They differ only in how the source enters:

- severance has no source term: no penalty at any level in any study;
- taint has one penalty per study, the same at None, Slight and Dramatic;
- discounting lets each study's penalty change in a straight line from None to
  Dramatic. Discounting predicts that the line falls; the model also allows it
  to rise, so its slope has to be read with it (section 5);
- the free shape lets each study's penalty take any value at each level.

Each model adds three parameters to the one before it, so they are nested: the
likelihood-ratio test compares each with the next simpler one by twice the
gain in log-likelihood (the log of the probability the model gives the data),
read against a chi-square distribution with three degrees of freedom, the
spread that quantity has when the three added terms are truly zero. AIC (the
Akaike information criterion) and BIC (the Bayesian information criterion)
score each model by its fit with a charge for each parameter; lower is better.
BIC's charge grows with the number of observations and is far heavier here, so
BIC favours simpler models than AIC does. The weights rescale each criterion
into a share of support among the four models that adds to one. The glosses
follow two rough conventions: for AIC differences, that of Burnham and
Anderson (2002), whose bands leave gaps between 2 and 4 and between 7 and 10
that are filled here; for BIC differences, that of Raftery (1995).

The free-shape model is the pooled model of section 4 written with the numeric
codes of section 3, and the run checks that the two give the same likelihood.
A comparison of four models on three studies describes which shape the data
sit closest to. It does not test a registered prediction.

```{r model-comparison}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("crossstudy_model_comparison.csv"))
CMP_CONTRASTS <- list(modification = "contr.sum", study = "contr.sum")
CMP_TERMS <- list(
  severance   = character(0),
  taint       = c("src", "src:st1", "src:st2"),
  discounting = c("src", "src:st1", "src:st2",
                  "src:modlin", "src:modlin:st1", "src:modlin:st2"),
  free        = c("src", "src:st1", "src:st2",
                  "src:modlin", "src:modlin:st1", "src:modlin:st2",
                  "src:modquad", "src:modquad:st1", "src:modquad:st2"))
CMP_TEXT <- vapply(CMP_TERMS, function(t) {
  paste("rating ~", paste(c("modification * study", t), collapse = " + "), "+", POOLED_RE)
}, character(1))
ACCOUNT <- c(severance = "severance", taint = "taint", discounting = "discounting",
             free = "free shape")
ALLOWS <- c(
  severance   = "no penalty at any level in any study",
  taint       = "one penalty per study, the same at every level",
  discounting = "a penalty per study that changes in a straight line from None to Dramatic",
  free        = "a penalty per study at each level, any shape")
LRT_QUESTION <- c(
  taint       = "Does one penalty per study, constant across the levels, improve on no penalty?",
  discounting = "Does letting the penalty change in a straight line improve on a constant penalty?",
  free        = "Does letting the penalty take any shape improve on a straight line?")

aic_gloss <- function(delta) {
  case_when(delta == 0 ~ "best by AIC",
            delta <= 2 ~ "close to the best by AIC: substantial support",
            delta <= 4 ~ "some support by AIC, less than the best",
            delta <= 7 ~ "considerably less support by AIC",
            delta <= 10 ~ "little support by AIC",
            TRUE ~ "essentially no support by AIC")
}
bic_gloss <- function(delta) {
  case_when(delta == 0 ~ "best by BIC",
            delta <= 2 ~ "weak evidence against it by BIC",
            delta <= 6 ~ "positive evidence against it by BIC",
            delta <= 10 ~ "strong evidence against it by BIC",
            TRUE ~ "very strong evidence against it by BIC")
}

cmp_fits <- list()
comparison <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  d <- data_by_measure[[m]]
  fits <- lapply(names(CMP_TERMS), function(k) {
    fit_lmm(as.formula(CMP_TEXT[[k]]), d, reml = FALSE, contrasts = CMP_CONTRASTS)
  })
  names(fits) <- names(CMP_TERMS)
  for (k in names(fits)) {
    log_fit(fits[[k]]$status, paste0("model comparison, ML: ", ACCOUNT[[k]]), m,
            CMP_TEXT[[k]], d)
  }
  # The free-shape model written with numeric codes equals the pooled model
  # written with factors, fitted by ML.
  factor_ml <- fit_lmm(POOLED_FORMULA, d, reml = FALSE, contrasts = SUM_CONTRASTS)
  log_fit(factor_ml$status, "model comparison, ML: pooled model with factor coding, a check",
          m, POOLED_TEXT, d)
  stopifnot(abs(as.numeric(logLik(factor_ml$fit)) -
                  as.numeric(logLik(fits$free$fit))) < 1e-3)
  cmp_fits[[m]] <<- fits

  ll   <- vapply(fits, function(f) as.numeric(logLik(f$fit)), numeric(1))
  npar <- vapply(fits, function(f) attr(logLik(f$fit), "df"), numeric(1))
  aic  <- vapply(fits, function(f) AIC(f$fit), numeric(1))
  bic  <- vapply(fits, function(f) BIC(f$fit), numeric(1))
  usable <- vapply(fits, function(f) fit_usable(f$status), logical(1))
  out <- tibble(measure = m, model = names(fits), account = unname(ACCOUNT),
                allows = unname(ALLOWS), formula = unname(CMP_TEXT),
                n_obs = nrow(d), n_parameters = npar, log_likelihood = ll,
                AIC = aic, BIC = bic) %>%
    mutate(delta_AIC = AIC - min(AIC), delta_BIC = BIC - min(BIC),
           AIC_weight = exp(-delta_AIC / 2) / sum(exp(-delta_AIC / 2)),
           BIC_weight = exp(-delta_BIC / 2) / sum(exp(-delta_BIC / 2)),
           compared_with = c(NA, "severance", "taint", "discounting"),
           lrt_question = c(NA, unname(LRT_QUESTION)),
           lrt_chisq = c(NA, 2 * diff(ll)),
           lrt_df = c(NA, diff(npar)),
           lrt_p = pchisq(lrt_chisq, lrt_df, lower.tail = FALSE),
           aic_reading = aic_gloss(delta_AIC),
           bic_reading = bic_gloss(delta_BIC),
           lrt_reading = case_when(
             is.na(lrt_p) ~ NA_character_,
             lrt_p < ALPHA ~ "yes: the gain in fit is larger than chance would give at .05",
             TRUE ~ "no: the gain in fit is within what chance would give at .05"),
           converged = usable[model],
           singular = vapply(fits, function(f) isTRUE(f$status$singular), logical(1)))
  # The likelihood-ratio tests equal those of lme4's anova() on the same fits.
  a <- anova(fits$severance$fit, fits$taint$fit, fits$discounting$fit,
             fits$free$fit, refit = FALSE)
  stopifnot(max(abs(a$Chisq[-1] - out$lrt_chisq[-1])) < 1e-6)
  # No reading rests on a fit that did not converge.
  if (!all(usable)) {
    out <- out %>% mutate(across(c(lrt_p, aic_reading, bic_reading, lrt_reading),
                                 ~ replace(.x, rep(TRUE, length(.x)), NA)))
  }
  out
}))
stopifnot(nrow(comparison) == 12, all(comparison$lrt_df[-c(1, 5, 9)] == 3))
write_table(comparison, "crossstudy_model_comparison.csv")
show_table(comparison %>% select(measure, account, n_parameters, log_likelihood,
                                 AIC, delta_AIC, AIC_weight, BIC, delta_BIC,
                                 BIC_weight, lrt_chisq, lrt_df, lrt_p),
           paste("Table 7.1. The four models of the source penalty, fitted by maximum",
                 "likelihood on the same rows. Each likelihood-ratio test compares a",
                 "model with the one above it. A description of which shape the data",
                 "sit closest to, not a test of a registered prediction."),
           digits = 3)
show_table(comparison %>% filter(!is.na(lrt_question)) %>%
             select(measure, lrt_question, lrt_reading, aic_reading, bic_reading),
           "Table 7.2. The model comparison in words.")
```

# 8. The penalty on original artworks

Creativity is the one measure rated for original artworks as well as second
works, so the creativity penalty on originals can stand beside the penalty on
second works. Two studies supply it. Study 1's registered H1 contrast, the
Human minus AI difference in creativity averaged over image kind (whether the
artwork shows a human or humanoid figure), is read from its deposited table;
its 95 percent interval is computed here from the standard error and degrees
of freedom in that table. Study 3 registered F tests, which ask whether a
factor's levels differ at all, and an equivalence test at 100 hours, not this
contrast, so its Human minus AI
difference averaged over stated time (the hours Alex is said to have spent on
the work) is recomputed here from its registered model, with the same formula,
contrasts and optimizer, and labelled as recomputed. The run checks that the
recomputed contrast reproduces Study 3's registered F test of source: for a
factor with two levels the F statistic is the square of the t statistic.

```{r originals}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("crossstudy_originals_reference.csv"))

# Study 1: the registered H1 contrast on creativity.
s1_family <- readr::read_csv(IN[["study1_family"]], show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
h1 <- s1_family %>% filter(hypothesis == "H1", grepl("creativity", test))
stopifnot(nrow(h1) == 1, round(h1$estimate, 3) == 0.448)
crit1 <- qt(0.975, h1$df)
study1_row <- tibble(
  study = "Study 1", artwork = "original", measure = "creativity",
  source_of_number = "registered H1 contrast, read from tables/study1_confirmatory_family.csv",
  contrast = "Human minus AI, averaged over image kind",
  estimate = h1$estimate, se = h1$se, df = h1$df, statistic = h1$statistic,
  p_two_sided = h1$p_raw,
  ci95_lo = h1$estimate - crit1 * h1$se, ci95_hi = h1$estimate + crit1 * h1$se,
  interval_note = "95 percent interval computed here from the table's standard error and degrees of freedom",
  n_participants = n_distinct(long[["Study 1"]]$id))

# Study 3: the registered creativity model, refitted.
d3 <- long[["Study 3"]] %>%
  filter(dimension == "creativity", !is.na(rating)) %>%
  mutate(Type = factor(Type, levels = SOURCE_LEVELS),
         time = factor(time, levels = c("under 1 hour", "10 hours", "100 hours")),
         id = factor(id), stimulus_id = factor(stimulus_id))
stopifnot(!anyNA(d3$Type), !anyNA(d3$time))
contrasts(d3$Type) <- contr.sum(2)
contrasts(d3$time) <- contr.sum(3)
S3_TEXT <- "rating ~ Type * time + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)"
s3 <- fit_with_status(lmerTest::lmer(as.formula(S3_TEXT), data = d3, REML = TRUE,
                                     control = lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))
log_fit(s3$status, "Study 3 registered model, refitted for the originals reference",
        "creativity", S3_TEXT, d3)
emm3 <- do.call(emmeans::emmeans, c(list(object = s3$fit, specs = ~ Type, data = d3), LMER_DF))
stopifnot(identical(as.character(emm3@grid$Type), SOURCE_LEVELS))
ct3 <- as_tibble(summary(emmeans::contrast(emm3, list("Human minus AI" = c(1, -1)),
                                           adjust = "none"),
                         infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), level = 0.95))

# The recomputed contrast reproduces Study 3's registered F test of source.
s3_f <- readr::read_csv(IN[["study3_ftests"]], show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE) %>%
  filter(dimension == "creativity", term == "Type")
stopifnot(nrow(s3_f) == 1, abs(ct3$t.ratio^2 - s3_f$F) / s3_f$F < 1e-4,
          abs(ct3$df - s3_f$den_df) < 1e-2)
cat("Study 3 recomputed t squared:", signif(ct3$t.ratio^2, 6),
    "| registered F of source:", signif(s3_f$F, 6), "\n")

study3_row <- tibble(
  study = "Study 3", artwork = "original", measure = "creativity",
  source_of_number = "recomputed here from Study 3's registered model (rating ~ Type * time + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), sum-to-zero contrasts, REML, bobyqa); not a registered contrast",
  contrast = "Human minus AI, averaged over stated time",
  estimate = ct3$estimate, se = ct3$SE, df = ct3$df, statistic = ct3$t.ratio,
  p_two_sided = na_unless_usable(ct3$p.value, s3$status),
  ci95_lo = na_unless_usable(ct3$lower.CL, s3$status),
  ci95_hi = na_unless_usable(ct3$upper.CL, s3$status),
  interval_note = "95 percent interval, Satterthwaite degrees of freedom; its t squared equals Study 3's registered F test of source",
  n_participants = n_distinct(d3$id))

originals <- bind_rows(study1_row, study3_row)
write_table(originals, "crossstudy_originals_reference.csv")
show_table(originals %>% select(study, contrast, estimate, se, df, ci95_lo, ci95_hi,
                                p_two_sided, source_of_number),
           "Table 8.1. The creativity penalty on original artworks, in rating points.")
```

# 9. The figures

```{r theme}
# The greyscale theme of Study 1's figures, with a legend at the foot, since
# these figures distinguish studies by the shape of their points.
theme_paper <- function(base_size = 11) {
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      legend.position    = "bottom",
      legend.title       = element_blank(),
      strip.background   = element_blank(),
      strip.placement    = "outside",
      strip.text         = element_text(size = base_size, face = "bold"),
      axis.line          = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
      axis.ticks         = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
      axis.text          = element_text(color = "black"),
      panel.grid         = element_blank(),
      plot.title         = element_text(size = base_size, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      plot.caption       = element_text(size = base_size - 2, color = "grey30",
                                        hjust = 0),
      plot.caption.position = "plot",
      plot.margin        = margin(8, 8, 8, 8))
}
# Each figure file states its status in a line at its foot, so a copy used on
# its own still says what it is.
FIG_STATUS <- paste("Exploratory analysis, specified after the registered results",
                    "were known; it changes no registered verdict.")

# Each series has its own point shape and grey. Open points are original
# artworks, grey points single studies of second works, and the black diamond
# the pooled estimate.
SERIES <- c("Study 1", "Study 3", "Study 2", "Study 4", "Study 5", "Pooled")
SERIES_LABELS <- c("Study 1" = "Study 1, originals", "Study 3" = "Study 3, originals",
                   "Study 2" = "Study 2", "Study 4" = "Study 4", "Study 5" = "Study 5",
                   "Pooled" = "Pooled, Studies 2, 4 and 5")
SERIES_SHAPES <- c("Study 1" = 21, "Study 3" = 25, "Study 2" = 21, "Study 4" = 22,
                   "Study 5" = 24, "Pooled" = 23)
SERIES_FILLS  <- c("Study 1" = "white", "Study 3" = "white", "Study 2" = "#A1A1A1",
                   "Study 4" = "#A1A1A1", "Study 5" = "#A1A1A1", "Pooled" = "black")
SERIES_SIZES  <- c("Study 1" = 2.2, "Study 3" = 2.2, "Study 2" = 2.2, "Study 4" = 2.2,
                   "Study 5" = 2.2, "Pooled" = 3)
# Points sit at x = 0 for originals and 1, 2 and 3 for None, Slight and
# Dramatic, each series shifted sideways so that the intervals do not overlap.
OFFSET <- c("Study 1" = -0.12, "Study 3" = 0.12, "Study 2" = -0.24,
            "Study 4" = -0.08, "Study 5" = 0.08, "Pooled" = 0.24)
LEVEL_X <- c(Original = 0, None = 1, Slight = 2, Dramatic = 3)

series_scales <- list(
  scale_shape_manual(values = SERIES_SHAPES, labels = SERIES_LABELS, breaks = SERIES),
  scale_fill_manual(values = SERIES_FILLS, labels = SERIES_LABELS, breaks = SERIES),
  scale_size_manual(values = SERIES_SIZES, labels = SERIES_LABELS, breaks = SERIES))

second_work_points <- function(m) {
  penalties %>%
    filter(measure == m) %>%
    transmute(series = ifelse(scope == "pooled", "Pooled", study),
              level = modification, estimate, ci95_lo, ci95_hi)
}
```

# 10. Robustness

## 10.1 An ordinal model of creativity

The linear model treats the five answers as evenly spaced numbers. A
cumulative-link mixed model instead treats them as ordered categories: it
estimates where the cut points between neighbouring answers fall on an
underlying scale, with a logistic curve for the chance of answering above each
cut point. The model has the same fixed and random terms as the pooled model,
with the participant and the second work entered as factors equal to
`study:id` and `image:modification`. The penalties are given on two scales: the
underlying scale itself, in logit units (the log of the odds of answering above
a cut point), and the expected rating in points,
computed for an average participant and second work (random effects at zero).
A fit counts as converged when the optimizer returns code 0 and raises no
warning about convergence or the Hessian (the matrix of second derivatives the
standard errors come from), as in Studies 1, 4 and 5; a singular fit is one
with a random-effect standard deviation below 0.0001. A fit that did not
converge keeps its estimates as description only, with no p-value or interval.

```{r ordinal}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("crossstudy_ordinal_check.csv"))
d_ord <- data_by_measure$creativity %>%
  mutate(rating_ord  = factor(rating, levels = 1:5, ordered = TRUE),
         participant = factor(paste(study, id, sep = ":")),
         work        = factor(paste(image, modification, sep = "_")))
ORD_TEXT <- paste("ordered rating ~ source * modification * study + (1 | study:id)",
                  "+ (1 | image) + (1 | image:modification), logit link, Laplace approximation")
fit_clmm <- function(d) {
  warns <- character(0)
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(
    tryCatch(ordinal::clmm(rating_ord ~ source * modification * study +
                             (1 | participant) + (1 | image) + (1 | work),
                           data = d, link = "logit", Hess = TRUE,
                           contrasts = SUM_CONTRASTS),
             error = function(e) e),
    warning = function(w) {
      warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    })
  failed <- inherits(fit, "error")
  list(fit = fit, data = d,
       status = tibble(
         fit_error = failed,
         converged = !failed && isTRUE(fit$optRes$convergence == 0) &&
           !any(grepl("converge|Hessian", warns, ignore.case = TRUE)),
         singular  = if (failed) NA else
           any(vapply(ordinal::VarCorr(fit), function(v) any(attr(v, "stddev") < 1e-4),
                      logical(1))),
         messages  = paste(unique(c(if (failed) conditionMessage(fit) else fit$optRes$message,
                                    warns)), collapse = " | ")),
       max_abs_gradient = if (failed) NA_real_ else max(abs(fit$gradient)))
}
t_ord <- system.time(ord <- fit_clmm(d_ord))
log_fit(ord$status, "ordinal check, creativity", "creativity", ORD_TEXT, d_ord,
        ord$max_abs_gradient)
cat("Cumulative-link fit:", round(t_ord[["elapsed"]]), "seconds | fit error",
    ord$status$fit_error, "| converged", ord$status$converged, "| singular",
    ord$status$singular, "| largest absolute gradient", signif(ord$max_abs_gradient, 3), "\n")
cat("Messages:", ord$status$messages, "\n")
if (!ord$status$fit_error) print(ordinal::VarCorr(ord$fit))

ordinal_scale <- function(mode, label) {
  if (ord$status$fit_error) {
    return(tibble(scale = label, modification = MOD_LEVELS, note = fit_note(ord$status)))
  }
  emm <- emmeans::emmeans(ord$fit, ~ source * modification * study, data = d_ord,
                          mode = mode)
  g <- as.data.frame(emm@grid)
  w <- setNames(lapply(MOD_LEVELS, function(l) penalty_w(g, l, DERIV_STUDIES)), MOD_LEVELS)
  rows <- contrast_rows(emm, w, ord$status)
  tibble(scale = label, modification = MOD_LEVELS) %>%
    bind_cols(select(rows, estimate, se, statistic, p_two_sided, ci95_lo, ci95_hi))
}
ordinal_check <- bind_rows(
  ordinal_scale("latent", "underlying scale, logit units"),
  ordinal_scale("mean.class", "expected rating in points, random effects at zero")) %>%
  left_join(penalties %>% filter(measure == "creativity", scope == "pooled") %>%
              select(modification, lmm_estimate = estimate, lmm_p = p_two_sided),
            by = "modification") %>%
  mutate(measure = "creativity", pooled_over = "Studies 2, 4 and 5, equal weights",
         same_direction_as_lmm = sign(estimate) == sign(lmm_estimate),
         converged = ord$status$converged, singular = ord$status$singular,
         max_abs_gradient = ord$max_abs_gradient,
         note = if (fit_usable(ord$status)) "" else
           "the fit did not converge under the rule, so its estimates are description only and carry no p-value or interval",
         model = ORD_TEXT, .before = 1)
stopifnot(nrow(ordinal_check) == 6)
write_table(ordinal_check, "crossstudy_ordinal_check.csv")
show_table(ordinal_check %>% select(scale, modification, estimate, se, statistic,
                                    p_two_sided, ci95_lo, ci95_hi, lmm_estimate),
           paste("Table 10.1. The pooled creativity penalty at each level from the",
                 "cumulative-link mixed model, beside the linear model's estimate in",
                 "rating points."))
```

## 10.2 Each study left out in turn

Each pooled model is fitted again three times per measure, each time without
one of the three studies, and the pooled penalty at each level is recomputed
over the two that remain, with equal weight. The table also says whether the
90 percent interval of each recomputed penalty still lies inside plus or minus
0.224.

```{r leave-one-out}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("crossstudy_leave_one_study_out.csv"))
loso <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  bind_rows(lapply(DERIV_STUDIES, function(out) {
    kept <- setdiff(DERIV_STUDIES, out)
    d <- data_by_measure[[m]] %>% filter(study %in% kept) %>% droplevels()
    res <- fit_lmm(POOLED_FORMULA, d, reml = TRUE, contrasts = SUM_CONTRASTS)
    log_fit(res$status, paste("leave one study out, REML, without", out), m,
            POOLED_TEXT, d)
    penalty_table(res, m, kept) %>%
      filter(scope == "pooled") %>%
      mutate(left_out = out, .after = measure)
  }))
})) %>%
  left_join(penalties %>% filter(scope == "pooled") %>%
              select(measure, modification, all_three_estimate = estimate),
            by = c("measure", "modification")) %>%
  mutate(change_from_all_three = estimate - all_three_estimate,
         interval_inside_bound = ci90_lo > -EQ_BOUND & ci90_hi < EQ_BOUND)
stopifnot(nrow(loso) == 27)
write_table(loso, "crossstudy_leave_one_study_out.csv")
show_table(loso %>% select(measure, left_out, modification, estimate, ci95_lo, ci95_hi,
                           p_two_sided, interval_inside_bound, all_three_estimate),
           paste("Table 10.2. The pooled penalty at each level with each study left",
                 "out in turn, beside the estimate from all three studies, in rating",
                 "points with 95 percent intervals."))
```

## 10.3 The pooled model against each study's registered estimates

The pooled model differs from each study's own model in two ways. Its terms
differ: it gives each second work its own baseline, which none of the studies'
models does, and it leaves out image kind and the time factors, which they
include. And it estimates one set of variances for the three studies together.
Its within-study penalties are therefore set beside the estimates each study
reported from its registered model: Study 2's exploratory source contrast at
each level, Study 4's secondary label effect at each level, and Study 5's
registered source contrast at each level. Each study is also fitted on its own
with the pooled model's terms,
`rating ~ source * modification + (1 | id) + (1 | image) + (1 | image:modification)`.
That fit splits each difference in two: the registered estimate and the
study-alone estimate differ only by the terms, and the study-alone estimate and
the pooled model's differ only by the shared variances.

```{r reconciliation}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("crossstudy_registered_reconciliation.csv"))
rd <- function(k) readr::read_csv(IN[[k]], show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
registered_by_level <- bind_rows(
  rd("study2_by_level") %>%
    transmute(study = "Study 2", measure, modification, registered_estimate = estimate,
              registered_table = "Study 2/tables/study2_source_by_modification.csv"),
  rd("study4_by_level") %>%
    transmute(study = "Study 4", measure, modification, registered_estimate = estimate,
              registered_table = "Study 4/tables/study4_secondary_label_by_modification.csv"),
  rd("study5_by_level") %>%
    transmute(study = "Study 5", measure = rating, modification,
              registered_estimate = estimate,
              registered_table = "Study 5/tables/study5_equivalence_source.csv"))
# Each study on its own, with the pooled model's terms.
ALONE_TEXT <- "rating ~ source * modification + (1 | id) + (1 | image) + (1 | image:modification)"
study_alone <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  bind_rows(lapply(DERIV_STUDIES, function(s) {
    d <- data_by_measure[[m]] %>% filter(study == s) %>% droplevels()
    stopifnot(identical(levels(d$source), SOURCE_LEVELS))
    res <- fit_lmm(as.formula(ALONE_TEXT), d, reml = TRUE,
                   contrasts = list(source = "contr.sum", modification = "contr.sum"))
    log_fit(res$status, paste(s, "on its own with the pooled model's terms, REML"), m,
            ALONE_TEXT, d)
    emm <- do.call(emmeans::emmeans, c(list(object = res$fit, specs = ~ source | modification,
                                            data = d), LMER_DF))
    ct <- as_tibble(summary(emmeans::contrast(emm, list("Human minus AI" = c(1, -1)),
                                              adjust = "none")))
    tibble(study = s, measure = m, modification = as.character(ct$modification),
           study_alone_estimate = ct$estimate, study_alone_usable = fit_usable(res$status))
  }))
}))

reconciliation <- penalties %>%
  filter(scope == "within study") %>%
  select(study, measure, modification, pooled_model_estimate = estimate) %>%
  inner_join(registered_by_level, by = c("study", "measure", "modification")) %>%
  inner_join(study_alone, by = c("study", "measure", "modification")) %>%
  mutate(difference = pooled_model_estimate - registered_estimate,
         from_model_terms = study_alone_estimate - registered_estimate,
         from_shared_variances = pooled_model_estimate - study_alone_estimate) %>%
  relocate(registered_table, .after = last_col())
stopifnot(nrow(reconciliation) == 27)
write_table(reconciliation, "crossstudy_registered_reconciliation.csv")
cat("Largest absolute difference:", signif(max(abs(reconciliation$difference)), 3),
    "| from the terms:", signif(max(abs(reconciliation$from_model_terms)), 3),
    "| from the shared variances:", signif(max(abs(reconciliation$from_shared_variances)), 3),
    "rating points\n")
show_table(reconciliation %>% select(study, measure, modification, registered_estimate,
                                     study_alone_estimate, pooled_model_estimate,
                                     difference, from_model_terms, from_shared_variances),
           paste("Table 10.3. Each study's penalty at each level in its own registered",
                 "table, from the study fitted on its own with the pooled model's terms,",
                 "and from the pooled model, in rating points. The difference splits",
                 "into the part the terms make and the part the shared variances make."),
           digits = 4)
```

## 10.4 The time factors of Studies 4 and 5

The pooled model averages over Study 4's source time and Study 5's editing
time. Whether that hides a difference depends on what each study's registered
tests found, which this section reads from their tables. It then refits each
study's registered model and gives the penalty at each time and level. The
refits reproduce each study's registered penalty at each level when averaged
over time, and the run checks that they do.

```{r time-check}
run_clear_outputs(run, table_path("crossstudy_time_check.csv"))

# The registered tests of the time factors.
time_tests <- bind_rows(
  rd("study4_family") %>%
    filter(test %in% c("source time", "source time by modification")) %>%
    transmute(study = "Study 4", measure, test, F = statistic, num_df, den_df, p_raw,
              p_holm, holm_significant),
  rd("study5_family") %>%
    transmute(study = "Study 5", measure = rating, test, F, num_df, den_df, p_raw,
              p_holm, holm_significant))
show_table(time_tests, paste("Table 10.4. The registered tests of the time factors,",
                             "read from each study's confirmatory table."))

# The registered models, refitted on each study's long data file.
time_fit <- function(study, m) {
  if (study == "Study 4") {
    d <- long[["Study 4"]] %>%
      filter(dimension == m, k_points == 5, !is.na(rating)) %>%
      transmute(id = factor(id), image = factor(source),
                source = factor(label, levels = SOURCE_LEVELS),
                time = factor(source_time, levels = c("less than 1 hour", "10 hours", "100 hours")),
                modification = factor(modification, levels = MOD_LEVELS), rating)
    text <- "rating ~ label * source_time * modification + (1 | id) + (1 | source)"
    f <- rating ~ source * time * modification + (1 | id) + (1 | image)
    con <- list(source = "contr.sum", time = "contr.sum", modification = "contr.sum")
  } else {
    d <- long[["Study 5"]] %>%
      filter(dimension == m, k_points == 5, !is.na(rating)) %>%
      transmute(id = factor(id), image = factor(image),
                source = factor(source, levels = SOURCE_LEVELS),
                time = factor(editing_time, levels = c("less than 1 hour", "10 hours", "100 hours")),
                modification = factor(modification, levels = MOD_LEVELS),
                image_kind = factor(image_kind, levels = c("NonFigure", "Figure")), rating)
    text <- "rating ~ source * editing_time * modification + image_kind + (1 | id) + (1 | image)"
    f <- rating ~ source * time * modification + image_kind + (1 | id) + (1 | image)
    con <- list(source = "contr.sum", time = "contr.sum", modification = "contr.sum",
                image_kind = "contr.sum")
  }
  stopifnot(!anyNA(d$source), !anyNA(d$time), !anyNA(d$modification))
  res <- fit_lmm(f, d, reml = TRUE, contrasts = con)
  log_fit(res$status, paste(study, "registered model, refitted for the time check"),
          m, text, d)
  emm <- do.call(emmeans::emmeans, c(list(object = res$fit,
                                          specs = ~ source | time * modification,
                                          data = d), LMER_DF))
  stopifnot(identical(as.character(unique(emm@grid$source)), SOURCE_LEVELS))
  ct <- emmeans::contrast(emm, list("Human minus AI" = c(1, -1)), adjust = "none")
  # The study name and the name of its time factor are set before the table
  # is built, so no column of the table can mask them.
  study_name  <- study
  time_factor <- if (study == "Study 4") "source time" else "editing time"
  as_tibble(summary(ct, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), level = 0.95)) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.character)) %>%
    transmute(study = study_name, measure = m, time_factor = time_factor,
              time, modification, estimate, se = SE, df,
              p_two_sided = na_unless_usable(p.value, res$status),
              ci95_lo = na_unless_usable(lower.CL, res$status),
              ci95_hi = na_unless_usable(upper.CL, res$status),
              model = text, converged = res$status$converged,
              singular = res$status$singular, note = fit_note(res$status))
}
time_check <- bind_rows(lapply(c("Study 4", "Study 5"), function(s) {
  bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(m) time_fit(s, m)))
}))
stopifnot(nrow(time_check) == 2 * 3 * 9)

# Averaged over time with equal weights, the refits give each study's
# registered penalty at each level.
time_avg <- time_check %>%
  group_by(study, measure, modification) %>%
  summarise(mean_over_time = mean(estimate), .groups = "drop") %>%
  inner_join(registered_by_level, by = c("study", "measure", "modification"))
stopifnot(nrow(time_avg) == 18,
          max(abs(time_avg$mean_over_time - time_avg$registered_estimate)) < 1e-6)

write_table(time_check, "crossstudy_time_check.csv")
show_table(time_check %>% filter(measure == "creativity") %>%
             select(study, time, modification, estimate, ci95_lo, ci95_hi, p_two_sided),
           paste("Table 10.5. The creativity penalty at each time and level in Studies",
                 "4 and 5, from each study's registered model refitted here, in rating",
                 "points with 95 percent intervals. The other two measures are in",
                 "tables/crossstudy_time_check.csv."))
```
