
# 12. What the numbers show

```{r summary-numbers}
# Every number in the prose below is read from the tables above, and every
# statement of direction or rank is checked here, so the knit stops if the
# prose would misstate a table.
# A value that rounds to zero prints without a minus sign. fp() prints a
# p-value alone and pv() prints it with its p, as "p = .017" or "p < .001".
fmt_num <- function(x, digits) {
  y <- round(x, digits)
  y[y == 0] <- 0
  formatC(y, format = "f", digits = digits)
}
f2 <- function(x) fmt_num(x, 2)
f3 <- function(x) fmt_num(x, 3)
fp <- function(p) if (is.na(p)) "NA" else if (p < 0.001) "< .001" else
  sub("^0", "", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3))
pv <- function(p) if (is.na(p)) "p = NA" else if (p < 0.001) "p < .001" else
  paste("p =", fp(p))
ci <- function(lo, hi) paste0("[", f2(lo), ", ", f2(hi), "]")

pen <- function(m, sc, l) {
  penalties %>% filter(measure == m, modification == l,
                       if (sc == "pooled") scope == "pooled" else study == sc)
}
trd <- function(m, sc, q) {
  trends %>% filter(measure == m, quantity == q,
                    if (sc == "pooled") scope == "pooled" else study == sc)
}
eqv <- function(m, l) equivalence %>% filter(measure == m, modification == l)
cmp <- function(m, k) comparison %>% filter(measure == m, model == k)
best <- function(m, crit) {
  x <- comparison %>% filter(measure == m)
  x$account[which.min(x[[crit]])]
}

pc <- setNames(lapply(MOD_LEVELS, function(l) pen("creativity", "pooled", l)), MOD_LEVELS)
slope_c <- trd("creativity", "pooled", "slope")
curv_c  <- trd("creativity", "pooled", "curvature")

# The statements the creativity prose makes.
stopifnot(
  all(equivalence$equivalent[equivalence$measure == "creativity"]),
  pc$None$estimate < pc$Slight$estimate, pc$None$estimate < pc$Dramatic$estimate,
  pc$None$p_two_sided > ALPHA, pc$Dramatic$p_two_sided > ALPHA,
  pc$Slight$p_two_sided < ALPHA,
  slope_c$p_two_sided > ALPHA, curv_c$p_two_sided < ALPHA,
  cmp("creativity", "taint")$lrt_p < ALPHA,
  cmp("creativity", "discounting")$lrt_p > ALPHA,
  cmp("creativity", "free")$lrt_p < ALPHA,
  best("creativity", "BIC") == "severance",
  best("creativity", "AIC") == "free shape",
  all(vapply(MOD_LEVELS, function(l) pen("creativity", "Study 4", l)$estimate < 0,
             logical(1))),
  pen("creativity", "Study 2", "Slight")$estimate > 0,
  pen("creativity", "Study 5", "Slight")$estimate > 0,
  pen("creativity", "Study 2", "Slight")$p_two_sided < ALPHA,
  pen("creativity", "Study 5", "Slight")$p_two_sided < ALPHA,
  all(originals$estimate > max(penalties$estimate[penalties$measure == "creativity" &
                                                    penalties$scope == "pooled"])))

# The statements about each study's shape. Study 2's penalty rises across the
# levels without a bend, Studies 4 and 5 carry the bend at Slight, Study 4's
# penalty is below zero at every level and Study 5's above it, Study 2's and
# Study 4's Dramatic penalties nearly cancel, only Studies 2 and 5 show a
# Slight penalty on their own, and in no study does the penalty fall
# significantly from None to Dramatic.
trc <- function(s, q) trd("creativity", s, q)
pnc <- function(s) vapply(MOD_LEVELS, function(l) pen("creativity", s, l)$estimate, numeric(1))
stopifnot(
  all(diff(pnc("Study 2")) > 0),
  trc("Study 2", "slope")$estimate > 0, trc("Study 2", "slope")$p_two_sided < ALPHA,
  trc("Study 2", "curvature")$p_two_sided > ALPHA,
  abs(trc("Study 2", "curvature")$estimate) <
    min(trc("Study 4", "curvature")$estimate, trc("Study 5", "curvature")$estimate),
  trc("Study 4", "curvature")$estimate > 0, trc("Study 5", "curvature")$estimate > 0,
  trc("Study 5", "curvature")$p_two_sided < ALPHA,
  all(pnc("Study 4") < 0), all(pnc("Study 5") > 0),
  pen("creativity", "Study 2", "Dramatic")$p_two_sided < ALPHA,
  pen("creativity", "Study 4", "Slight")$p_two_sided > ALPHA,
  abs(pnc("Study 2")[3] + pnc("Study 4")[3]) < 0.25 * pnc("Study 2")[3],
  slope_c$ci95_lo < 0,
  all(!(trends$estimate < 0 & trends$p_two_sided < ALPHA &
          trends$quantity == "slope" & trends$measure == "creativity")))

# The two qualifications the creativity prose names: only leaving out Study 4
# takes a creativity penalty past the bound, and Study 5's creativity penalty
# is largest in its 10-hour cell at every level.
loso_outside <- loso %>% filter(measure == "creativity", !interval_inside_bound)
s5_peak_time <- time_check %>%
  filter(study == "Study 5", measure == "creativity") %>%
  group_by(modification) %>% slice_max(estimate, n = 1) %>% ungroup()
stopifnot(nrow(loso_outside) > 0, all(loso_outside$left_out == "Study 4"),
          all(s5_peak_time$time == "10 hours"))
```

**Creativity.** On creativity, the pooled penalty on a second work is
`r f2(pc$None$estimate)` rating points at None `r ci(pc$None$ci95_lo, pc$None$ci95_hi)`,
`r f2(pc$Slight$estimate)` at Slight `r ci(pc$Slight$ci95_lo, pc$Slight$ci95_hi)` and
`r f2(pc$Dramatic$estimate)` at Dramatic `r ci(pc$Dramatic$ci95_lo, pc$Dramatic$ci95_hi)`.
At every level its 90 percent interval lies inside plus or minus 0.224, so at
no level does the pooled penalty reach half of the penalty Study 1 found on
originals. Only the Slight penalty differs from zero (`r pv(pc$Slight$p_two_sided)`,
uncorrected). On originals the penalty was `r f2(originals$estimate[1])` in Study 1
`r ci(originals$ci95_lo[1], originals$ci95_hi[1])` and `r f2(originals$estimate[2])`
in Study 3 `r ci(originals$ci95_lo[2], originals$ci95_hi[2])`, larger than the
pooled penalty at any level of second work.

The penalty does not fall as Alex changes more. Its slope is
`r f3(slope_c$estimate)` points per step `r ci(slope_c$ci95_lo, slope_c$ci95_hi)`,
an interval that leaves room for a fall of at most
`r f2(-slope_c$ci95_lo)` points per step, and it is smallest at None, where
discounting predicts it is largest. Its one departure from a flat line is a
bend at Slight: the Slight penalty sits `r f2(curv_c$estimate)` points above
the mean of the other two `r ci(curv_c$ci95_lo, curv_c$ci95_hi)`.

The three studies do not share that shape. In Study 2 the penalty rises with
modification, `r f2(pnc("Study 2")[1])`, `r f2(pnc("Study 2")[2])` and
`r f2(pnc("Study 2")[3])` points at None, Slight and Dramatic (slope
`r f3(trc("Study 2", "slope")$estimate)` per step, `r pv(trc("Study 2", "slope")$p_two_sided)`),
with no bend (curvature `r f2(trc("Study 2", "curvature")$estimate)`,
`r pv(trc("Study 2", "curvature")$p_two_sided)`); its Dramatic penalty differs
from zero on its own (`r pv(pen("creativity", "Study 2", "Dramatic")$p_two_sided)`).
The bend comes from Studies 4 and 5, whose Slight penalties sit
`r f2(trc("Study 4", "curvature")$estimate)` and `r f2(trc("Study 5", "curvature")$estimate)`
points above the mean of their other two
(`r pv(trc("Study 4", "curvature")$p_two_sided)` and
`r pv(trc("Study 5", "curvature")$p_two_sided)`). Study 4's penalties lie below
zero at every level (`r paste(f2(pnc("Study 4")), collapse = ", ")`) and Study 5's
above it (`r paste(f2(pnc("Study 5")), collapse = ", ")`). In no study does the
penalty fall significantly from None to Dramatic.

The model comparison says the same. A constant penalty per study improves on
none (likelihood-ratio chi-square(3) = `r f2(cmp("creativity", "taint")$lrt_chisq)`,
`r pv(cmp("creativity", "taint")$lrt_p)`), but that model lets the
penalty differ by study, and Study 4's runs the other way at every level, so the
gain does not show one penalty shared by the three studies. A straight-line
change adds nothing to a constant penalty (chi-square(3) =
`r f2(cmp("creativity", "discounting")$lrt_chisq)`,
`r pv(cmp("creativity", "discounting")$lrt_p)`), and a free shape improves on the
straight line (chi-square(3) = `r f2(cmp("creativity", "free")$lrt_chisq)`,
`r pv(cmp("creativity", "free")$lrt_p)`). AIC ranks the `r best("creativity", "AIC")`
model first, with weight `r f2(max(comparison$AIC_weight[comparison$measure == "creativity"]))`;
the taint model has weight `r f2(cmp("creativity", "taint")$AIC_weight)` and
severance `r f2(cmp("creativity", "severance")$AIC_weight)`. BIC, which charges
more for each parameter, ranks severance first, with weight
`r formatC(cmp("creativity", "severance")$BIC_weight, format = "f", digits = 4)`.

Read against the three accounts, the data do not show the shape discounting
predicts: no significant fall from None to Dramatic, pooled or in any study,
and the smallest pooled penalty where discounting expects the largest. They do not fit
taint well either: whatever penalty is constant across the levels is less than
half of Study 1's, and the penalty is not constant but bends at Slight. Pooled,
they sit closest to severance, with no penalty to speak of at None or Dramatic,
and depart from it at one level, a small penalty at Slight that reaches
significance on its own in two of the three studies. The pooled picture rests
on studies that disagree: Study 2's penalty grows with modification and Study
4's runs below zero, and the two cancel at Dramatic. The support for any one
account is weak: AIC and BIC disagree on the best model, and a comparison of
four models on three studies describes the data rather than testing a
registered prediction. The None level, which the memorandum expected to decide
among the accounts, sits near the bottom of the scale (mean creativity
`r f2(pc$None$human_mean)` under the Human label and `r f2(pc$None$ai_mean)`
under AI), so a penalty there has little room to show, and the missing penalty
at None counts against discounting less than it would on a level with room to
move.
Two checks in section 10 qualify this reading: the bound holds at every level
only with Study 4 in the pool, and Study 5's penalty comes mostly from one of
its editing times. The paragraphs on robustness and on the time factors below
give the numbers.

```{r summary-other-measures, results='asis'}
# The other two measures, in the same terms, generated from the tables. The
# slope of each study is given with its direction, because the straight-line
# model allows the penalty to rise as well as fall, and only a fall is the
# shape discounting predicts.
slope_words <- function(m) {
  s <- trends %>% filter(measure == m, quantity == "slope", scope == "within study")
  falls <- s$study[s$estimate < 0 & s$p_two_sided < ALPHA]
  rises <- s$study[s$estimate > 0 & s$p_two_sided < ALPHA]
  paste0("Within each study the slope is ",
         paste(sprintf("%s (%s, %s)", f3(s$estimate), s$study,
                       vapply(s$p_two_sided, pv, character(1))), collapse = ", "),
         ". ",
         if (length(falls) == 0) "In no study does the penalty fall significantly, the direction discounting predicts" else
           paste0("The penalty falls significantly in ", paste(falls, collapse = " and ")),
         if (length(rises) == 0) "." else
           paste0("; it rises significantly in ", paste(rises, collapse = " and "),
                  ", the opposite direction."))
}
for (m in c("transformativeness", "essence_change")) {
  p <- setNames(lapply(MOD_LEVELS, function(l) pen(m, "pooled", l)), MOD_LEVELS)
  e <- setNames(lapply(MOD_LEVELS, function(l) eqv(m, l)), MOD_LEVELS)
  s <- trd(m, "pooled", "slope")
  cat(sprintf(paste0(
    "**%s.** The pooled penalty is %s points at None %s (%s), %s at Slight %s (%s) ",
    "and %s at Dramatic %s (%s). Its pooled slope across the levels is %s points per ",
    "step %s. %s Likelihood-ratio tests: constant penalty against none, %s; ",
    "straight line against constant, %s; free shape against straight line, %s. ",
    "AIC ranks the %s model first and BIC the %s model.\n\n"),
    MEASURE_LABELS[[m]],
    f2(p$None$estimate), ci(p$None$ci95_lo, p$None$ci95_hi), e$None$reading,
    f2(p$Slight$estimate), ci(p$Slight$ci95_lo, p$Slight$ci95_hi), e$Slight$reading,
    f2(p$Dramatic$estimate), ci(p$Dramatic$ci95_lo, p$Dramatic$ci95_hi), e$Dramatic$reading,
    f3(s$estimate), ci(s$ci95_lo, s$ci95_hi), slope_words(m),
    pv(cmp(m, "taint")$lrt_p), pv(cmp(m, "discounting")$lrt_p), pv(cmp(m, "free")$lrt_p),
    best(m, "AIC"), best(m, "BIC")))
}

# Where the pooled penalty peaks on each measure.
peak <- penalties %>% filter(scope == "pooled") %>%
  group_by(measure) %>% slice_max(estimate, n = 1) %>% ungroup()
none_pooled <- penalties %>% filter(scope == "pooled", modification == "None")
ranks_agree <- all(vapply(MEASURES, function(m) {
  best(m, "AIC") == "free shape" && best(m, "BIC") == "severance"
}, logical(1)))
if (all(peak$modification == "Slight") && ranks_agree &&
    all(none_pooled$p_two_sided > ALPHA)) {
  cat(sprintf(paste(
    "**Across the three measures.** On every measure the pooled penalty is largest",
    "at Slight and near zero at None (no more than %s points either way, none",
    "different from zero), and on every measure AIC ranks the free shape first while",
    "BIC ranks severance first. A penalty concentrated at the level of colour and",
    "contrast adjustments is the pattern these data show; none of the three accounts",
    "predicted it.\n\n"), f2(max(abs(none_pooled$estimate)))))
} else {
  cat("**Across the three measures.** The pooled penalty peaks at",
      paste(sprintf("%s on %s", peak$modification, peak$measure), collapse = ", "), ".\n\n")
}
```

```{r summary-robustness, results='asis'}
# The robustness checks, in words, generated from the tables.
oc <- ordinal_check %>% filter(scale == "underlying scale, logit units")
stopifnot(oc$modification[which.max(oc$estimate)] == "Slight")
ord_code <- if (ord$status$fit_error) NA_integer_ else as.integer(ord$fit$optRes$convergence)
cat(sprintf(paste0(
  "**Robustness.** The cumulative-link model of creativity %s. Its penalties on the ",
  "underlying scale are %s, %s and %s logit units at None, Slight and Dramatic, in the ",
  "same direction as the linear model's at %d of 3 levels and with the same peak at ",
  "Slight. The pooled model's within-study penalties differ from each study's ",
  "registered estimates by at most %s points on any measure. Fitting each study ",
  "on its own with the pooled model's terms splits that difference: the terms ",
  "(a baseline added for each second work; image kind and the time factors left ",
  "out) move an estimate by at most %s points, and sharing the variances across ",
  "the studies moves it by at most %s.\n\n"),
  if (fit_usable(ord$status)) "converged" else if (isTRUE(ord_code == 0))
    paste("did not converge under the rule: its optimizer returned code 0, but the",
          "update of the random effects inside each step warned that it had not",
          "converged (the warnings are in crossstudy_fit_status.csv), so its",
          "estimates are description only") else
    paste("did not converge under the rule (the warnings are in",
          "crossstudy_fit_status.csv), so its estimates are description only"),
  f2(oc$estimate[1]), f2(oc$estimate[2]), f2(oc$estimate[3]),
  sum(oc$same_direction_as_lmm),
  f3(max(abs(reconciliation$difference))),
  f3(max(abs(reconciliation$from_model_terms))),
  f3(max(abs(reconciliation$from_shared_variances)))))

# Leaving out each study in turn, on creativity.
lc <- loso %>% filter(measure == "creativity")
lo_text <- vapply(DERIV_STUDIES, function(s) {
  x <- lc %>% filter(left_out == s) %>% arrange(match(modification, MOD_LEVELS))
  out <- x$modification[!x$interval_inside_bound]
  sprintf(paste0("Without %s the pooled creativity penalty is %s, %s and %s at None, ",
                 "Slight and Dramatic (uncorrected p-values %s, %s and %s); %s. %s"),
          s, f2(x$estimate[1]), f2(x$estimate[2]), f2(x$estimate[3]),
          fp(x$p_two_sided[1]), fp(x$p_two_sided[2]), fp(x$p_two_sided[3]),
          if (length(out) == 0) "every 90 percent interval stays inside plus or minus 0.224" else
            paste0("the 90 percent interval at ", paste(out, collapse = " and "),
                   " reaches past 0.224"),
          if (which.min(x$estimate) == 1) "The penalty is still smallest at None." else
            "The penalty is then not smallest at None.")
}, character(1))
cat("**Each study left out.**", paste(lo_text, collapse = " "), "\n\n")

# The time factors, in words, generated from the registered tables and the
# refits of section 10.4.
t4 <- time_tests %>% filter(study == "Study 4")
t5 <- time_tests %>% filter(study == "Study 5")
t5_sig <- t5 %>% filter(holm_significant)
tests_text <- sprintf(paste(
  "**The time factors.** In Study 4, %d of its %d registered tests of source time",
  "survived Holm's correction, the adjustment each study registered for running",
  "several tests at once. In Study 5, %d of its %d registered tests of editing",
  "time survived: %s."),
  sum(t4$holm_significant), nrow(t4), sum(t5$holm_significant), nrow(t5),
  if (nrow(t5_sig) == 0) "none" else
    paste(sprintf("%s on %s (Holm-corrected %s)", t5_sig$test, t5_sig$measure,
                  vapply(t5_sig$p_holm, pv, character(1))), collapse = "; "))

# The Study 5 creativity penalty at each editing time and level.
tc5 <- time_check %>% filter(study == "Study 5", measure == "creativity")
TIMES <- c("less than 1 hour", "10 hours", "100 hours")
at <- function(l, t) tc5$estimate[tc5$modification == l & tc5$time == t]
by_time <- function(l) {
  sprintf("%s, %s and %s", f2(at(l, TIMES[1])), f2(at(l, TIMES[2])), f2(at(l, TIMES[3])))
}
creativity_interaction <- any(t5_sig$measure == "creativity" &
                                t5_sig$test == "source by editing time")
grid_text <- sprintf(paste(
  "%s At None the Study 5 creativity penalty is %s at less than 1 hour, 10 hours and",
  "100 hours; at Slight %s; at Dramatic %s."),
  if (creativity_interaction)
    "So the Study 5 creativity penalty differs across editing times, and the pooled curve averages over that difference." else
    "The pooled curve averages over editing time.",
  by_time("None"), by_time("Slight"), by_time("Dramatic"))

ten_largest <- all(vapply(MOD_LEVELS, function(l) {
  which.max(vapply(TIMES, function(t) at(l, t), numeric(1))) == 2
}, logical(1)))
n_by_time <- long[["Study 5"]] %>% distinct(id, editing_time) %>% count(editing_time)
ten_text <- if (ten_largest) sprintf(paste(
  "At every level the 10-hour cell carries the largest penalty, so Study 5's",
  "contribution to the pooled curve comes mostly from the participants told that",
  "Alex spent 10 hours on the second work. Editing time varied between",
  "participants, each time with its own group of %d to %d people, so this is a",
  "difference between groups of people as well as between stated times."),
  min(n_by_time$n), max(n_by_time$n)) else ""
cat(paste(tests_text, grid_text, ten_text), "\n\n")
```

# 13. Session information and the run manifest

```{r session-info}
SESSION_PATH  <- table_path("crossstudy_sessionInfo.txt")
VERSIONS_PATH <- table_path("crossstudy_package_versions.csv")
run_clear_outputs(run, SESSION_PATH, VERSIONS_PATH)
writeLines(c(paste("Analysis status:", ANALYSIS_STATUS), "",
             capture.output(sessionInfo())), SESSION_PATH)
pkgs <- c("readr", "dplyr", "tidyr", "tibble", "jsonlite", "Matrix", "lme4",
          "lmerTest", "emmeans", "ordinal", "ggplot2", "rmarkdown", "knitr")

                   version = vapply(pkgs, function(p) as.character(packageVersion(p)),
                                    character(1))),
            basename(VERSIONS_PATH))
sessionInfo()
```

```{r manifest}
# The manifest lists every output this run registered, whether this run
# wrote it, and its SHA-256 checksum. It is written last. It is then written
# again with the analysis status as its last column; it does not list itself,
# so the second write changes no checksum in it.
manifest <- write_run_manifest(run)
stopifnot(all(manifest$written_this_run))
write_table(manifest, basename(run$manifest_path))
```
